To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there are differences between the perceptions of older adults and nurses regarding the older adult’s ADL and IADL functioning upon discharge, and that the social network of older adults has a positive impact on their perceptions of IADI functioning upon discharge.

1) there is agreement between older adult patients and nurses on the quality of life upon discharge, 2) there is disagreement between older adult patients’ and nurses’ perceptions of the patients’ functional ability upon discharge, and 3) social network and social support are related to functional ability upon discharge.

there are areas of agreement and of disagreement between older adult patients and nurses about discharge needs, with nurses perceiving patients as being less independent than patients perceived themselves to be; that patients’ perceived independence with respect to ADIs upon discharge was associated with their social networks and quality of life; and that patients’ perceived IADL independence upon discharge was associated positively with their overall social network and friend subscale scores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an instrument to measure the impact of case management on the quality of life of older adults.
the identification of the needs of older people who have been hospitalized, and the development of a model of care that meets those needs.
the identification of areas of agreement and/or disagreement between nursing staff members and older adult patients regarding discharge needs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings of this study indicate the need for nurses to be more sensitive to patients’ perceptions of their ADL and IADL abilities and to include patients in the discharge planning process.

older patients are more independent in ADLs than nurses think they are, that older patients are as independent as nurses think they are with respect to IADLs and QOL, and that older patients’ social networks have an effect on their IADL independence and QOL.

the study results indicated that patients and nurses had similar perceptions of patients’ ADL independence upon discharge from the hospital, but nurses perceived patients’ IADLs as being less independent than did patients themselves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the older adult patients and nurses agreed that older adult patients were able to perform most ADLs independently upon discharge from the hospital.
the older adult patients in our study perceived themselves to be more independent than the nurses did.
older adult patients and their nurses agree on the quality of life and independence with respect to ADLS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nurses should be aware of the importance of social support in facilitating the transition to the home environment for hospitalized older adults.
nurses need to understand that patients’ self-reported ADL and IADL independence upon discharge may not reflect the actual level of independence they have.
older adult patients’ and nurses’ perceptions of patients’ discharge ADL and IADL independence and quality of life are often different.
